cards.front: Which moon is the largest in the whole solar system?
cards.back: Ganymede, one of Jupiter's moons. It is bigger than the planet Mercury.

cards.front: Which moon has a thick atmosphere and lakes of liquid methane?
Which of Jupiter's moons is the most volcanically active place we know?
cards.back: Io. Tidal squeezing from Jupiter and its neighbours keeps its volcanoes erupting.

cards.front: Which Jovian moon is thought to hide an ocean under its icy shell?
cards.back: Europa. It is one of the best places to look for life beyond Earth.

cards.front: Which moon of Jupiter is covered in old, heavily cratered ice?
Which Saturnian moon shoots geysers of water ice from its south pole?
Which Saturn moon looks like the Death Star because of one giant crater?
Which Saturn moon is two-toned, dark on one side and bright on the other?
Which small Saturn moon looks like a sponge and tumbles chaotically?
Which Neptune moon orbits backwards and was probably captured?
cards.back: Triton. It also has nitrogen geysers.

cards.front: What is the biggest moon of Uranus?
Which Uranian moon has huge cliffs, like Verona Rupes?
Which moons of Uranus are named after characters in Shakespeare and Pope?
cards.back: All of them: Titania, Oberon, Ariel, Umbriel, Miranda, and more.

cards.front: Which dwarf planet's biggest moon is almost half its size?
How many moons does Mars have?
Which moon of Mars is the larger, and is slowly spiralling inwards?
What is the name of Earth's only natural satellite?
Which planets have no moons at all?
Which planet is known to have the most moons?
cards.back: Saturn, and the count keeps growing as telescopes improve.

cards.front: Which four moons did Galileo discover in 1610?
cards.back: Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto, the Galilean moons.

cards.front: Who discovered Titan in 1655?
What are Jupiter's four big moons collectively called?
Which moon is bigger than Mercury but has less than half its mass?
Which Saturn moon is the second largest in the solar system?
Which moon is the only one with a dense atmosphere and a landing by a probe (Huygens)?
What causes the heat that keeps Io's volcanoes active?
cards.back: Tidal flexing, as Jupiter's gravity squeezes and stretches it.

cards.front: Why is Triton's orbit special?
cards.back: It goes backwards (retrograde) around Neptune, so it was probably captured from the outer solar system.

cards.front: What mainly causes Earth's ocean tides?
cards.back: The Moon's gravity pulling on the oceans (the Sun adds a smaller pull).

cards.front: Which Saturn moon sits in the E ring and feeds it with ice from its geysers?
Which two moons orbit Mars?
cards.back: Phobos (fear) and Deimos (dread), named for two sons of Ares, the Greek god of war.
